title: USDA safe minimum internal cooking temperatures
description: Minimum internal temperatures by product, with rest times, as published by USDA FSIS, plus the danger zone.
authority: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS)

provenance.source: USDA FSIS — Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart
provenance.note: Page states 'Last Updated: Apr 14, 2025'. Every row below reproduces that table verbatim, including the exact Celsius values FSIS prints (62.8 / 71.1 / 73.9 / 60 °C), which are the Fahrenheit figures converted, not independently rounded.

The 40–140 °F range is taken from the section title as listed in FSIS navigation on 2026-08-27; the page body could not be re-fetched here because fsis.usda.gov returns 403 to non-browser clients. Treat the range as stable (it is long-standing USDA guidance) and re-check the page itself before republishing at scale.

rows.product: Beef, pork, veal and lamb — steaks, chops and roasts
rows.note: Remove from heat, then allow to rest for at least 3 minutes before carving or consuming.
rows.source: USDA FSIS — Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart
rows.quote: Beef, Pork, Veal and Lamb Steaks, Chops and Roasts | 145 degrees F (62.8 degrees C) and allow to rest for at least 3 minutes

rows.note: Cook, then rest at least 3 minutes.
rows.source: USDA FSIS — Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart
rows.quote: Ham, Fresh or Smoked (Uncooked) | 145 degrees F (62.8 degrees C) and allow to rest for at least 3 minutes

rows.source: USDA FSIS — Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart
rows.quote: Fish & Shellfish | 145 degrees F (62.8 degrees C)

rows.note: Ground product is not covered by the rest-time rule.
rows.source: USDA FSIS — Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart
rows.quote: Ground Meats | 160 degrees F (71.1 degrees C)

rows.note: USDA lists 160 °F for eggs; cook until yolk and white are firm.
rows.source: USDA FSIS — Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart

rows.note: 140 °F (60 °C) for hams packaged in USDA-inspected plants; 165 °F (73.9 °C) for all others.
rows.source: USDA FSIS — Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart
rows.quote: Fully Cooked Ham (to Reheat) | Reheat cooked hams packaged in USDA-inspected plants to 140 degrees F (60 degrees C) and all others to 165 degrees F (73.9 degrees C).

rows.product: All poultry — breasts, whole bird, legs, thighs, wings, ground poultry, giblets and stuffing
rows.note: USDA also lists 'Ground Poultry' as a separate row at 165 degrees F; this row's parenthetical already includes ground poultry, so the value is identical.
rows.source: USDA FSIS — Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart
rows.quote: All Poultry (Breasts, Whole Bird, Legs, Thighs, Wings, Ground Poultry, Giblets and Stuffing) | 165 degrees F (73.9 degrees C)

rows.source: USDA FSIS — Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart

rows.note: Reheat to 165 °F (73.9 °C) as measured with a food thermometer.
rows.source: USDA FSIS — Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart

dangerZone.rule: Keep food out of this range: refrigerate promptly, and do not leave perishable food at room temperature for more than 2 hours (1 hour above 90 °F / 32 °C).

notes: These are minimum internal temperatures measured with a food thermometer in the thickest part, not oven settings. Oven temperature and doneness are different things.
Consumers may cook to higher temperatures for personal preference; USDA states the values above are the minimums.
Celsius values are exactly what USDA prints. Where a recipe rounds 145 °F to 63 °C or 165 °F to 74 °C, that is the same rule rounded — do not treat the rounding as a different threshold.
This dataset covers USDA-regulated meat, poultry, egg and fish products. Produce and other categories are outside FSIS's table and are deliberately not included.
